statement: Fix ν > 0 smaller than p − b in the applicable row of (2.5). For all sufficiently large w and R ≥ Cw, a function F of that parity, supported in Bw(z), satisfies ∥PR,zF◦ ∥∞ ≤ C(w/R)b ∥F∥∞ , (2.10) ∥PR,zF◦ − ℓb(F)PR,zOb(z)∥∞ ≤ C(w/R)p−ν ∥F∥∞ . (2.11) In particular, the second bound is the improved decay bound for a function of charge zero. We shall use ν = 1/4. The exponent 3 − ν requires the individual even function to be invariant under right-angle rotations; invariance of its probability law alone does not suffice. For a site at fixed positive relative distance from the cutting contour, ∥PR,ze(y)∥∞ ≤ CR−1 , ∥PR,zσy∥∞ ≤ CR−d . (2.12) The first bound also holds for a single plane-centered bond product.
